standard.title: Discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.description: use play, imagination, arts knowledge, processes and/or skills to discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have experience with free play and exploration of materials, voice, movement and basic digital devices. They have not yet deliberately used play as a strategy for discovering creative possibilities in media arts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use play, imagination and arts processes to discover new possibilities and develop ideas for media arts works.

nodes.label: Playing to discover
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can engage in purposeful play with materials, movement, voice or technology and notice what happens — identifying at least one discovery or surprise.
nodes.minimum_width: Engage with one material, movement quality, or technology in free play — identify one thing they discovered or that surprised them.
nodes.typical_width: Explore multiple materials and technologies through play (tactile materials, camera, voice, movement); respond to the emotions or discoveries that arise; describe how different qualities (rough, smooth, loud, quiet) could be used to communicate ideas.
wider: Play with the tactile qualities of materials and use movement, voice or digital tools to embody the qualities discovered — connecting sensory exploration to idea generation
Respond to music through movement — using scarves, drawing or digital capture to document the response and discussing how the music changed what was discovered
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot engage in purposeful discovery through play, the idea-development strand of this standard collapses — play is the primary mechanism for generating ideas at Foundation level.

response_modes.reason: Vary the play contexts — tactile materials, digital tools, voice, movement — to ensure students discover possibilities across the full range of media arts modalities available at Foundation.

success_criteria: Student can describe or demonstrate something they discovered while playing with a material, tool or technology
Student can name at least one way this discovery could be used to communicate an idea

nodes.label: Imagining possibilities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use imagination to extend what they observe or know — asking 'what if?' questions to develop new ideas for arts works.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one imagining strategy (asking 'What happens next?', taking the point of view of a character, or imagining an environment) to extend an observed story or situation.
nodes.typical_width: Use imagination to explore how characters in stories might look, move or speak; make still or moving images to communicate ideas about characters; ask questions of stories to develop new scenarios; improvise rhythms, movements or melodies and interpret them visually.
wider: Imagine and trial ways to use geometric and organic shapes creatively — collage, movement traces of shapes, or melodies that follow a shape's contour; exploring multiple representations of the same shape
Use a camera to document a process (e.g. mixing colours, building a structure) — sequence and annotate the images as a record of imaginative problem-solving
Explore speaking and singing voices to discover new ways to communicate ideas and feelings — experimenting with pitch, volume, rhythm and tone

response_modes.reason: Build students' repertoire of imagining strategies — 'What happens next?', character perspective, environment transformation. A wider repertoire means more generative possibilities when making.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of imaginative entry points at Foundation is genuinely rich — character POV, environmental transformation, voice exploration, shape interpretation. Students who access multiple strategies have a much broader creative toolkit.
success_criteria: Student can use at least one imagining strategy to extend a story, character or situation beyond what was given
Student can describe the new possibility they imagined

nodes.label: Developing and documenting ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can translate discoveries from play and imagination into a developing idea for an arts work — using a tool, material or device to record or represent the idea.
nodes.minimum_width: Use one tool or material to document or represent a developing idea (e.g. capture images that show steps in a process, draw a character imagined during play, record a voice improvisation).
nodes.typical_width: Use multiple tools and documentation strategies to develop ideas across sessions — capture image sequences of processes, draw from imaginative play, improvise and record rhythmic patterns; describe how the documentation connects to their original discovery or imaginative exploration.
wider: Improvise movement sequences to explain steps in a process, then use a camera to capture an image story that can be displayed to remind others about the process
Improvise rhythmic patterns and interpret them visually using drawing, collage or digital image-making — cross-modal translation as an idea development strategy

response_modes.reason: Documenting ideas integrates the play/discovery phase with the making phase — support students in connecting what they found through play to a concrete representation that others can see or hear.

success_criteria: Student creates or captures something that represents an idea developed through play or imagination
Student can explain the connection between their play/exploration and the developing idea
